keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# minor is the relative minor of A major

mainProgression.description: Hypnotic two-chord oscillation that creates the song's dreamy, ambiguous atmosphere through simple minor-to-flat-seven movement

sectionProgressions.description: The clean-tone riff outlines the F#m to E movement with a single-note descending and ascending pattern
The distorted chorus opens up the harmonic palette with power chords, adding the A and B for intensity
Darker harmonic territory using the IV and bVI chords for building tension before the solo

harmonicFunction: F#m (i) - Tonic minor establishing the song's dark, introspective center
E (bVII) - Flat seventh providing forward motion without dominant tension
A (bIII) - Relative major chord adding brightness in the chorus
B (IV) - Subdominant providing harmonic lift in chorus and bridge
D (bVI) - Flat sixth adding darker color in bridge sections

techniques.name: Clean Tone Single-Note Riff
techniques.description: The iconic opening riff played on the low strings with a clean chorus-effected tone, using a simple descending and ascending pattern that outlines the F#m-E harmony

notes: The riff uses notes on the low E string (D string in Drop D context) and A string
Practice the main riff pattern at a slow tempo
In Drop D tuning played on the D and A strings
All notes are played as even 8th notes with consistent dynamics
The chorus effect adds shimmer and width to the clean tone
Let each note ring slightly into the next for a legato feel
sequence: Set the guitar to the neck pickup with chorus effect engaged
Play the open string, then ascend: fret 2, fret 4, fret 5
At the top of the pattern, reverse direction: fret 5, fret 4, fret 2, open
Repeat the ascending-descending pattern in a continuous loop
Maintain even 8th-note timing throughout the riff
tips: Use alternate picking (down-up-down-up) for even note articulation
Keep the fretting fingers close to the fretboard for quick, clean movement
The chorus effect is essential - without it, the riff loses its character
Practice very slowly at first to ensure every note is clean and even
The riff should feel hypnotic and meditative, not rushed
details.progression: Single-note riff outlining F#m - E movement

techniques.name: Dynamic Contrast (Clean vs Distorted)
techniques.description: Switching between the quiet, chorus-effected clean verse tone and the loud, distorted chorus tone - the hallmark of the grunge quiet-loud dynamic

notes: The verse uses clean tone with chorus effect for the single-note riff
The chorus kicks in distortion for power chords and aggressive strumming
Use a distortion or overdrive pedal toggled on for chorus sections
The transition should be abrupt and dramatic - not gradual
Guitar volume knob can also control the clean-to-dirty transition
sequence: Play the clean riff through the verse with chorus effect
At the transition to chorus, stomp the distortion pedal on
Switch from single-note riff to full power chord strumming
At the verse return, cut the distortion and return to clean single notes
Maintain this dynamic shift consistently throughout the song
tips: Practice the pedal switching in time so there is no gap in the music
The emotional impact comes from the contrast - make the clean parts really clean
Don't use too much gain on the distortion - a moderate crunch is authentic
Practice the switch between single-note riff and power chords separately
details.progression: Clean: F#m - E riff, Distorted: F#m - A - B power chords

techniques.name: Chorus Effect Usage
techniques.description: Applying the chorus pedal effect to create the shimmering, watery clean tone that defines the song's atmospheric verse sections

notes: The chorus effect doubles the signal with slight pitch modulation
Set the rate (speed) to slow-to-medium for a gentle shimmer
Set the depth to moderate - not too extreme or wobbly
The mix should be around 50% wet for balanced blending
A Small Clone or Boss CE-2 style chorus captures the Nirvana tone
sequence: Engage the chorus pedal before the song begins
Set rate to 9-10 o'clock position for slow modulation
Set depth to 12 o'clock for moderate effect
Play the clean riff and adjust until the tone matches the recording
Disengage the chorus when switching to distortion for the loud sections
tips: Kurt Cobain used an Electro-Harmonix Small Clone chorus pedal
Too much depth makes the tone seasick - start subtle
The chorus effect should make the clean tone shimmer, not wobble
If you don't have a chorus pedal, a slight flanger on slow setting can approximate it
details.progression: Applied to the clean F#m - E riff sections

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The song opens with the iconic clean, chorus-drenched single-note riff that descends and ascends on the low strings, immediately establishing the hypnotic mood
notes: This is the signature hook - every note must be clean and even
Use the neck pickup with chorus effect for the authentic tone
Alternate picking keeps the 8th notes consistent
The riff repeats four times before the verse vocals enter

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse continues the same clean riff underneath Kurt Cobain's subdued vocal melody, maintaining the atmospheric and introspective mood
notes: The riff remains identical to the intro throughout the verse
Keep the dynamics controlled - the verse should stay quiet and restrained
Lock in with the bass, which plays a similar pattern an octave lower
The hypnotic repetition is intentional - resist the urge to add ornamentation

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus explodes with distorted power chords, dramatically shifting from the quiet verse with aggressive strumming and the signature vocal hook
notes: Kick in the distortion pedal right at the chorus transition
Use Drop D power chord shapes - one finger barring across three strings
Strum aggressively with full downstrokes for maximum impact
The contrast with the quiet verse is the emotional core of this song

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: The bridge builds tension with sustained B and D power chords over a darker harmonic palette, leading into the guitar solo
notes: Sustained power chords with heavy distortion and feedback
Let each chord ring for a full measure before changing
Build intensity through the bridge to lead into the solo
The D5 chord in Drop D uses the open bottom string for a massive, low tone

sections.name: Solo
sections.description: The solo is essentially the main riff played with distortion and doubled, maintaining the song's commitment to melody over technical showmanship
notes: The solo follows the same melodic contour as the main riff
Played with distortion rather than the clean chorus tone of the verse
It's doubled (two guitar tracks playing the same thing) for thickness
This is a great beginner solo because it uses the same notes as the riff

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The outro repeats the chorus progression with increasing intensity and feedback, building to the final distorted climax before cutting off
notes: The outro builds intensity through repetition and increasing aggression
Allow some feedback and noise for authentic grunge character
The final chord should ring out and sustain with feedback
The song ends with the distortion still ringing into silence

alternatives: Any single-coil or humbucker-equipped electric guitar
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup for the clean riff, bridge pickup for distorted sections; single coils preferred

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or small combo amp (Fender Champ)
alternatives: Any clean amp with good headroom

settings.bass: 6 (full low end for Drop D tuning)

effects.distortion: Boss DS-1 or DS-2 Turbo Distortion for the chorus sections, moderate gain setting
effects.reverb: Subtle spring reverb from the amp, nothing excessive
effects.other: Electro-Harmonix Small Clone chorus pedal is essential for the clean verse tone; set to slow rate and moderate depth

beginner.focus: Learn the main riff pattern and basic power chord shapes in Drop D tuning
steps: Tune to Drop D (lower the 6th string from E to D)
Learn the ascending-descending single-note riff on the A string
Practice the riff with even 8th-note timing at 90 BPM
Learn the basic Drop D power chord shapes for the chorus (F#5, A5, B5)

intermediate.focus: Master the clean-to-distorted dynamic transitions and full song structure
steps: Practice switching between clean riff and distorted power chords
Work on the bridge section B5-D5 chord changes
Play through the entire song form with proper dynamic contrast
Add the chorus effect to the clean sections and practice pedal switching

advanced.focus: Perfect the tone, add the solo, and capture the authentic grunge atmosphere
steps: Dial in the authentic Nirvana chorus-clean and distorted tones
Learn the guitar solo (doubled riff with distortion)
Master seamless transitions between all song sections
Perform the full song with emotional dynamics and controlled feedback

commonMistakes: Forgetting to tune to Drop D before playing - the riff doesn't work in standard tuning
Playing the riff notes unevenly - each 8th note should be the same duration
Using too much distortion gain, which muddies the power chords in Drop D
Making the clean-to-distorted transition too gradual instead of dramatic
practiceRoutine: Tune to Drop D and warm up with the single-note riff slowly at 80 BPM
Practice the riff at gradually increasing tempos up to 120 BPM
Work on Drop D power chord shapes and transitions for 10 minutes
Practice the clean-distorted switching with pedals at song tempo
Play through the complete song with a backing track or metronome
focusAreas: Even 8th-note articulation in the main riff
Drop D power chord voicings and smooth chord changes
Chorus effect pedal settings and tone matching
metronomeWork: Start at 80 BPM playing the single-note riff with alternate picking
Increase to 100 BPM focusing on keeping all 8th notes perfectly even
At 110 BPM, add the power chord chorus sections between riff repetitions
Reach target tempo of 120 BPM with the full song dynamics
